option.name: displayContent
option.value:
If the **Users file is inside `Data`**, then your program must open it using the correct relative path.
For example, if your project structure is like:
```text Project1 - Utility library/ ├── Data/ │ └── Users.text ├── cmake-build-debug/ │ └── ATMSystem ```
and your program is running from:
```text cmake-build-debug/ ```
then this path:
```cpp "Data/Users.text" ```
will **not work**, because the program will look for:
```text cmake-build-debug/Data/Users.text ```
not:
```text Project1 - Utility library/Data/Users.text ```
## Fix option 1: copy `Data` into `cmake-build-debug`
Make sure you have:
```text cmake-build-debug/Data/Users.text ```
Then this kind of path works:
```cpp "Data/Users.text" ```
## Fix option 2: use `../Data/Users.text`
If your executable runs from:
```text Project1 - Utility library/cmake-build-debug/ ```
and your `Data` folder is here:
```text Project1 - Utility library/Data/ ```
then the relative path should be:
```cpp "../Data/Users.text" ```
because `..` means “go one folder back”.
So in your users class, the filename should be something like:
```cpp const string UsersFileName = "../Data/Users.text"; ```
or:
```cpp static string _FileName = "../Data/Users.text"; ```
depending on how your code is written.
## Also check the exact filename
You wrote **Useres**, but make sure the real file name is exactly what your code uses:
```text Users.text ```
not:
```text Useres.text Users.txt users.text ```
Linux is strict about this.
## Why login fails
Your program probably tries to open something like:
```text Users.text ```
or:
```text Data/Users.text ```
from the build folder.
But the actual file is probably here:
```text ../Data/Users.text ```
So the file is not opened, the users list becomes empty, and then `User1 / 1234` is rejected.

Also, because you run from the build folder:
```text cmake-build-debug/ ```
a relative path like:
```cpp "Data/Users" ```
may still fail unless the working directory is the project root.
## Best fix
Use an absolute path from CMake, like you already started doing for clients.

Your current definition has two problems:
```cmake CLIENTS_FILE_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/data/Clients.txt" ```
But your folder is:
```text Data ```
not:
```text data ```
and your file is:
```text Clients.text ```
not:
```text Clients.txt ```
On Linux, case and extensions matter.
Use this instead:
<llm-snippet-file>CMakeLists.txt</llm-snippet-file> ```cmake # ... existing code ... target_compile_definitions(ATMSystem PRIVATE CLIENTS_FILE_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/Data/Clients.text" USERS_FILE_PATH="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/Data/Users" ) ```

if (MyFile.is_open()) { // ... existing code ... static clsUser Find(string UserName, string Password) {
fstream MyFile; MyFile.open(USERS_FILE_PATH, ios::in);//read Mode
if (MyFile.is_open()) { // ... existing code ... ```

option.name: displayContent
option.value:
The build is successful. This message is **not from your C++ code**:
```text Error running 'ATMSystem' Debugger executable not specified Configure ```
It means your IDE does not know which debugger to use.
On Linux, you need to configure a debugger like:
```text gdb ```
or:
```text lldb ```
## Fix on Linux
### 1. Install `gdb`
Open terminal and run:
```bash sudo apt update sudo apt install gdb ```
Then check it:
```bash gdb --version ```
You should see the installed GDB version.
---
## 2. Configure debugger in the IDE
In JetBrains CLion / C++ IDE:
1. Go to **File** 2. Open **Settings** 3. Go to:
```text Build, Execution, Deployment > Toolchains ```
4. Find the **Debugger** field. 5. Set it to:
```text /usr/bin/gdb ```
Usually the full path is:
```text /usr/bin/gdb ```
If you are not sure, run:
```bash which gdb ```
Example output:
```text /usr/bin/gdb ```
Use that path in the debugger field.
---
## 3. Apply and rerun debug
After setting the debugger:
1. Click **Apply** 2. Click **OK** 3. Run Debug again.
---
## Important: your code built successfully
This part confirms build is OK:
```text [2/2] Linking CXX executable ATMSystem Build finished ```
The warnings are not the reason debugging failed. They are code warnings, but the debugger problem is only IDE configuration.
---
## About the warnings
You also have warnings like:
```text warning: no return statement in function returning non-void ```
These should be fixed later, but they do **not** cause:
```text Debugger executable not specified ```
Main issue now:
```text Debugger is not configured in the IDE. ```

You are on **CachyOS**, which is Arch-based, not Ubuntu/Debian.
So `apt` will not work.
Use `pacman` instead.
## Install GDB on CachyOS / Arch
Run:
```bash sudo pacman -Syu gdb ```
Then check:
```bash gdb --version ```
To find the path:
```bash which gdb ```
Usually it will be:
```text /usr/bin/gdb ```
## Then configure the debugger
In your IDE:
```text File > Settings > Build, Execution, Deployment > Toolchains ```
Set **Debugger** to:
```text /usr/bin/gdb ```
Then apply and debug again.
## If you prefer LLDB
You can also install LLDB:
```bash sudo pacman -Syu lldb ```
Then check:
```bash which lldb ```
But for your case, `gdb` is enough.

option.name: displayContent
option.value:
Yes, I see it.
Your debugger is now set to:
```text /usr/bin/gdb ```
but the IDE shows this warning:
```text Version: 17.2; supported versions are 7.8.x–16.3.x ```
So the problem is:
```text Your GDB is too new for your IDE version. ```
You installed **GDB 17.2**, but your IDE supports only up to **GDB 16.3.x**.
## Best fix: update your IDE
The cleanest solution is to update CLion / JetBrains IDE to a newer version that supports GDB 17.
If you installed it with JetBrains Toolbox, update it from Toolbox.
If you installed it from CachyOS/Arch packages, run:
```bash sudo pacman -Syu ```
Then restart the IDE.
## Alternative fix: use LLDB instead
Install LLDB:
```bash sudo pacman -Syu lldb ```
Then check its path:
```bash which lldb ```
Usually:
```text /usr/bin/lldb ```
Then in the IDE debugger field, select:
```text /usr/bin/lldb ```
This may work better than downgrading GDB.
## Not recommended: downgrade GDB
You could install an older GDB version, but on Arch/CachyOS this is annoying and can break package consistency.
So use one of these:
1. **Update the IDE** — best option. 2. **Use LLDB** — good alternative.
## Summary
Your setup is almost correct. The remaining issue is only version compatibility:
```text GDB 17.2 > IDE supported max 16.3 ```
Update the IDE or switch debugger to LLDB.
